thread:
maria: Hey team — ran the apples-to-apples harness after the kernel selection change. Seeing unexpected tail latency spikes for multi-tenant runs. :eyes:
aj: What flavour of run? replay or synth?
maria: Replay of production traces + a light Poisson jitter overlay. Also did a pure synth run for baseline. Results diverged.
devin: Can you paste the top-level numbers?
maria: Sure — replay: p95 jumped from 48ms -> 220ms for tenant group B. synth: p95 stayed ~52ms. KV cache hit-rate in replay dropped from 92% -> 64% around the regression window.
sophie: That smells like KV cache churn + kernel swap interacting with batching. Did the kernel selector choose a different matmul path for long prompts?
maria: Yes, kernel selector moved some sequences to Kernel-B (int8-friendly) after the swap. Kernel-B has slightly higher per-token overhead for short sequences, but scales better at large batch sizes.
aj: So with replay, arrival patterns create microbursts that force small batches but trigger Kernel-B via sequence-length heuristic?
devin: Exactly — we hit a threshold in the selector that uses median seq len across coalesced requests. For microbursts the heuristic flips unexpectedly.
maria: I captured a small trace. Repro gist: https://internal.gist/replay-regression-1942 (logs + flamegraphs).
bench-bot: Automated regression detector flagged this run as Sev4: latency_tail_increase, diff p95 +> 3x, kvcache_drop.
sophie: Proposed quick checks: 1) force kernel to Kernel-A for a run, 2) lower batch_size_cap to 32, 3) drop max_delay_ms to 8. Want to run all combos in the harness.
aj: Agreed. Also try synthetic workload with identical inter-arrival jitter overlay so it's apples-to-apples. Our synth generator supports overlaying a JS distribution.
maria: Running permutations now. Command I'm using:
```bash
./harness/run_bench --mode=replay \
  --trace=prod_jan12.json \
  --overlay=jitter_poisson:lambda=50ms \
  --kernel-force=auto|Kernel-A|Kernel-B \
  --batch-cap=32,64,128 \
  --max-delay-ms=8,20,50 \
  --collect=kv_hits,latency_hist,arena_alloc
```
aj: Nice. Make sure to set tenant-weights to match prod: --tenant-mix=0.6:0.3:0.1 (A:B:C).
maria: Added. First quick run results (summary): Kernel-A + batch_cap=32 + max_delay=8 -> p95 56ms, KV hit 91%. Kernel-B + batch_cap=128 + max_delay=50 -> p95 240ms, KV hit 65%.
devin: That isolates it: Kernel-B + big batch cap + high delay allows the scheduler to build large batches but kernel overhead + KV misses kill tail.
sophie: For fairness: tenant B was getting starved when we allowed larger max_delay because tenant A's requests batched ahead and consumed cache. We need per-tenant batch caps or fairness-preserving delay caps.
aj: Suggest experiment: per-tenant max_delay_ms and a small global batch cap. e.g., tenant B max_delay_ms=8, tenant A=50. See if p95 for B recovers without hurting overall throughput.
maria: Ran that: per-tenant caps improved B's p95 to 70ms while A's p95 stayed ~60ms and throughput dropped only 3%. KV hit for B recovered to 88%.
devin: Good tradeoff. Also want to try a selector tweak: prefer Kernel-A if median_seq_len < 64 AND current_kv_hit < 80%. That might avoid flips when cache is cold.
sophie: Another idea: change the selector hysteresis — require a 10s stable signal before switching kernels for a worker. That will reduce flapping during microbursts.
aj: Both sound reasonable. Need to be careful with rollout impact on cost. Kernel-A is costlier per token at high batch but avoids tail spikes.
maria: Agreed. I'll prepare a small eval harness comparing 10min runs for 4 configs: (1) current selector, (2) selector + hysteresis, (3) per-tenant caps, (4) selector + per-tenant caps. Collect kv_hits, p50/p95/p99, and request-fairness index.
bench-bot: Scheduled: eval-1942003333-compare-configs, ETA 35m. Will notify when done.
ops-bot: FYI — I created an incident ticket INC-2026-042 to track mitigation and customer impact.
sophie: For the benchmark methodology note: we should document the harness differences that caused the synth vs replay gap: synth was missing inter-request locality (same user sending many correlating prompts), and no tenant-weight skew. Add that to runbook.
aj: Also add guidance: "when validating kernel selector changes, always run replay with jitter overlay + at least one synth config with overlayed tenant skew".
maria: Writing up the runbook now. I'll paste draft below when ready. Quick ask: anyone oppose landing a selector hysteresis + per-tenant caps as a conservative default?
devin: +1 from infra.
sophie: +1 from runtime.
aj: +1 but add metrics guardrail to rollback if throughput drops >10% or cost/k-token rises >12%.
maria: Great — I'll open the PR with test harness results and the rollout plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:
